newsitem.title: INDIA: India tribal militants kill 12 Hindus.
newsitem.headline: India tribal militants kill 12 Hindus.

text.p: Tribal guerrillas killed 12 Hindus, executing six after tying them to a tree, in a series of attacks on villages in northeastern India, police said on Tuesday.
Members of the National Democratic Front of Bodoland (NDFB) kidnapped seven Bengali-speaking Hindus in the Rangiya area of Assam state late on Monday.
The militants took them to a forest in Tuslibari, about 40 km (25 miles) west of Guwahati city near the Bhutanese border.
They tied the hostages to a tree and fired assault rifles at them, police in Guwahati said. Six were killed and the seventh was seriously wounded and now in hospital, they said.
In a second incident, militants from the same group fired on Hindus in Hatimora village in the Rangiya area on Monday night, killing four people, police said.
The NDFB, created in 1985 and formerly called the Bodo Security Force, wants an independent homeland for 600,000 Bodos carved out of the oil- and tea-rich state.
The guerrillas have their camps in the foothills of southern Bhutan and accuse Bengali-speaking Hindu immigrants of encroaching on their homeland in Assam.
In a third attack, guerrillas from an unidentified group late on Monday killed two Hindus in Nikasi village near Rangiya.
The NDFB and other guerrilla groups have recently stepped up their separatist campaigns.

On Monday, suspected guerrillas of the Bodoland Liberation Tigers Force set off a bomb by remote control on a rail track in Assam. Six coaches were derailed in the blast, which police said occurred several minutes before the Delhi-bound Rajdhani Express carrying 400 passengers reached the spot. No one was injured.
Bodo guerrillas have killed 11 people in the past two weeks in Assam with remote-control bombs. At least 33 people died last December when Bodo extremists bombed a train.
Monday's attack comes ahead of a planned 36-hour general strike from Wednesday in support of a call by Bodo student groups campaigning for a separate Bodoland.
